snp5.19:1.2: Per SnA, once their questions were answered the sixteen brahmans requested and received the Going-forth and Acceptance. Afterward Piṅgiya — now Ven. Piṅgiya — asked and received the Buddha’s permission to return to Bāvarī and report on their trip.
snp5.19:1.5: Following the Sri Lankan and Burmese readings, nikkāmo nibbano nāgo (the Thai has nibbuto, “unbound,” for nibbano; the PTS has nātho, “protector,” for nāgo) — a reading Nd II confirms. Per Nd II, “no forest” here means free of the “forests” of passion, aversion, delusion, resentment, and the rest of the unskillful mental fabrications; see Dhp 283.
snp5.19:5.5: The clause “and gave me no pleasure” appears in the Thai edition but not in the others.
snp5.19:16.1: Per Nd IIA, “showing conviction” means reaching arahantship through the strength of conviction — though the phrase seems to carry a broader sense at SN 6:1. Ven. Vakkali’s story is told at SN 22:87; at AN 1:147 (1:208) the Buddha names him foremost among the monks in being decisive through conviction. This Bhadrāvudha appears to be the same one from Sn 5:12; Āḷavi Gotama isn’t mentioned anywhere else in the Canon.
snp5.19:18.1: At AN 8:71 (AN 8:64 by the PTS count) the Buddha says he didn’t claim full awakening until his knowledge of the deva world was complete.
